{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-8","id":"msg_011CeCa7Z5m1YbfKXZtuQ8eS","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01GQkDTJn95r66r39iRCohBb","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/ssd/workspace/buidlguidl/ethskills-evals-test/artifacts/frontend-playbook-quiz-004/2026-08-19T181913Z-claude-with-skill-3/workspace/answer.md","content":"# Why the static export broke on Node 25\n\nShort version: **Node grew a `localStorage`.** Code in the app tree used\n\"does `localStorage` exist?\" as its proxy for \"am I in a browser?\" That proxy\nwas true for a decade and quietly became false. The prerender now runs\nbrowser-only code against a server-side `localStorage` that isn't a real\nbrowser `Storage`, and it blows up.\n\n---\n\n## 1. What actually changed in Node\n\nNode added the **Web Storage API** (`localStorage` / `sessionStorage`) as real\nglobals:\n\n- **Node 22.4.0** introduced them experimentally behind\n  `--experimental-webstorage`.\n- Newer majors (the 24/25 line your CI just jumped to) move this toward\n  **on by default**, so `globalThis.localStorage` is now a defined global\n  during a plain `node`/`next build` run — no flag, no browser.\n\nThe practical consequence is one line of truth flipping:\n\n```js\n// Node 20/older:      \"undefined\"\n// Node 25 (default):  \"object\"   ← the whole bug\ntypeof localStorage\n```\n\nI verified the surrounding behavior on the Node 22 line locally:\n\n- With the feature enabled but no backing file, the `localStorage` global is a\n  lazy getter that **throws** on first access\n  (`ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE: '--localstorage-file' ... Received ''`).\n- With `--localstorage-file` set, `typeof localStorage.getItem === \"function\"`\n  and it round-trips normally.\n- `--no-experimental-webstorage` is accepted and forces `typeof localStorage`\n  back to `\"undefined\"`.\n\nSo the server-side `localStorage` is not a friendly browser `Storage`. Depending\non how it's configured (or which SSR storage shim a dependency selects now that\nthe global is truthy), reaching for it during a build yields either a throw or\nan object that doesn't carry the method you called — which is exactly your\n`localStorage.getItem is not a function`. The common root is the same: **the\nexistence check that used to gate this code no longer means what the author\nthought it meant.**\n\n---\n\n## 2. Why Teammate A is out of date\n\nA's claim — *\"Node has no localStorage, so there's nothing to call `getItem`\non, the error is impossible\"* — was correct **through Node 20**. It's a\npre-22.4 fact.\n\nThe error isn't impossible; it's the *direct symptom* of A being wrong.\n`localStorage` is now a global in the build process. Some code guarded a\nbrowser-only path with `typeof localStorage !== \"undefined\"` (or `if\n(localStorage)`), that guard now passes on the server, the path executes during\nprerender, and it calls a method that isn't there. A is reasoning about a Node\nthat CI no longer runs.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Why Teammate B's polyfill *cannot* work — where the prerender runs\n\nB's fix is aimed at the wrong problem in the wrong place.\n\n**Wrong problem.** A polyfill answers \"localStorage is missing, add it.\" But\n`localStorage` is *not* missing — it already exists (that's §1). You can't fix\n\"the global exists and is unsuitable\" by adding a global.\n\n**Wrong place — and this is the decisive part.** Ask what the failure tells us:\nB wrote a *correct* `localStorage` and the build **fails identically**. If B's\npolyfill were installed in the same scope where the page renders, a correct\n`getItem` would satisfy the call and the error would *change or disappear*. It\ndidn't budge. That is hard evidence that **the polyfill never executes in the\nscope that renders the page.**\n\nHere's why. `next build` with `output: \"export\"` doesn't prerender pages in the\nmain build process. It fans work out to **separate render workers** (jest-worker\nprocesses/threads), each with its **own fresh global scope**. `instrumentation.ts`'s\n`register()` is designed to run once when a *server runtime* boots; it is not a\nreliable hook for the static-export render workers, and even where it does run\nit can fire after the offending module graph has already been pulled in. So the\nmodule that touches `localStorage` evaluates in a worker where B's `register()`\nnever ran — the polyfill simply isn't there.\n\nNet: **no matter how correct the polyfill is, it's being installed in a process\nthat isn't the one doing the prerender.** `instrumentation.ts` is structurally\nthe wrong lever for build-time static generation.\n\n(`/_not-found` shows up as the failing page because it's one of the always-on\nroutes Next prerenders; the real offender is shared provider/wallet code that\nruns on every route.)\n\n---\n\n## 4. What actually fixes it\n\nThe bug is *browser-only code executing during prerender*. Fix that, don't\nfake the browser.\n\n1. **Fix the guard (root cause).** Detect the browser with something that is\n   *still* browser-only. `window` remains `undefined` in Node:\n\n   ```js\n   // was:  if (typeof localStorage !== \"undefined\")   ← now true on the server\n   if (typeof window !== \"undefined\") {\n     window.localStorage.getItem(/* ... */);\n   }\n   ```\n\n2. **Never touch storage during render.** Read/write `localStorage` inside\n   `useEffect`, event handlers, or lazy init — never at module top-level or in a\n   render body. Server render and prerender must not read storage at all.\n\n3. **Make storage-touching components client-only.** For wallet/provider\n   components that reach for storage on import (wagmi/RainbowKit/connectkit\n   config, theme restore, etc.), load them with\n   `dynamic(() => import(\"./X\"), { ssr: false })`, or use the standard SE2\n   `mounted` gate (render nothing until a `useEffect` sets `mounted`). If this\n   used to work in SE2, something recently slipped *outside* that gate — that's\n   where to look.\n\n4. **Unblock CI immediately (band-aid, not a fix).** Restore the old world so\n   the guard behaves: pin the build to a Node LTS where the global is off, or\n   disable the feature explicitly:\n\n   ```bash\n   NODE_OPTIONS=--no-experimental-webstorage yarn build\n   ```\n\n   This makes `typeof localStorage === \"undefined\"` again and the build passes —\n   but it's papering over code that shouldn't run server-side. Do #1–#3 so the\n   app is correct regardless of which Node CI runs next.\n\n---\n\n### One-paragraph summary\n\nRecent Node added a real `localStorage` global (experimental in 22.4, trending\non-by-default by 24/25), so `typeof localStorage` flipped from `undefined` to\ndefined. Browser-detection code that keyed off that now runs during prerender\nand calls into a server-side `localStorage` that isn't a working browser\n`Storage`. A is quoting a pre-Node-22 fact. B's polyfill can't help because\n(a) the global already exists and (b) Next's static export renders pages in\nseparate worker processes that never run `instrumentation.ts`'s `register()`,\nso the polyfill lands in the wrong scope — proven by the *identical* failure.\nThe fix is to stop running storage code during prerender: guard on `window`,\ndefer storage to `useEffect`, and load wallet/provider components with\n`ssr: false`; pinning Node or `--no-experimental-webstorage` is only a stopgap.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":3935,"cache_read_input_tokens":21387,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":3935},"output_tokens":3,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"de9c0958-325b-4479-874f-ddf8ec584bdc","uuid":"752b23b6-0ca1-43bf-a9fa-151fec1526fd","timestamp":"2026-08-19T18:22:26.227Z","request_id":"req_011CeCa7W1Tw1Ggc7usMnWQQ"}
